title: Thin Air — Altitude Pace Calculator
description: A race-pace calculator that keeps goal time and pace in two-way sync, then applies a clearly labelled altitude model from sea level up to Leadville's 10,152 ft. It builds even or negative split tables, draws a mountain-style pace profile in SVG and prints a race wristband.
prompt: Build me 'Thin Air', an altitude-aware running pace calculator — a nod to my Mile High Run Club site. Distance presets for 5K, 10K, half and full plus a custom distance with a km/mi toggle; goal time and pace should stay in two-way sync. Add an altitude slider from sea level to Leadville (10,152 ft) with an approximate adjustment model that's honestly labelled as a rule of thumb. Output a split table with an optional negative split, an elevation-style SVG chart of the pace profile, and a printable wristband strip. Validate every input with friendly, specific errors. One self-contained HTML file, no external requests, and it has to look great on a phone.

methodology: Functional oracles computed by hand: 10K in 50:00 must read 5:00/km and 8:03/mi; half at 5:00/km must back-fill 1:45:29.
Model check: the labelled formula 0.1% × (thousands of ft)² is asserted at Denver (+2.8%, 1:45:00 → 1:47:56) and at the slider max (+10.3%).
Invariant test for negative splits: first split slower than last, yet the final elapsed time still equals the goal exactly.
Negative-path validation: malformed clocks, out-of-range minutes and negative distances must show friendly errors, set aria-invalid and keep the last good plan.
Output consistency: wristband cells and the split table's last elapsed time must agree with the adjusted finish time.
Responsive review at 1280px and 390px for the split table, SVG chart and horizontally scrollable wristband.
risks: Rounding drift between pace × distance and the displayed total when switching units.
Partial final split (e.g. 0.21 mi) mislabelled or mis-timed.
Two-way sync loops or stale values when both fields are edited in sequence.
Print stylesheet hiding or clipping the wristband.
qa.playwright: Everything here is deterministic arithmetic, so the spec asserts exact strings (1:47:56, 8:03, +10.3%) rather than approximate ranges. Inputs commit on Enter/change, so fill() + press('Enter') mirrors real use on both the desktop and touch profiles. The range input is driven by focusing it and pressing End, which exercises the keyboard path instead of injecting a value. Printing itself isn't automated (window.print opens a dialog); the spec asserts the wristband DOM that the print stylesheet isolates instead. No screenshots were needed because every visual output has a text or testid oracle.
coverage: Time → pace sync and km ↔ mi re-expression with a partial last split
Altitude presets and slider driving the labelled penalty model
Negative split shape with preserved finish time

a11y: All controls are native buttons, inputs and a labelled range slider; distance and unit chips expose aria-pressed and the slider's aria-valuetext includes the penalty. Errors use role=alert, invalid fields get aria-invalid, and the result stats sit in an aria-live region.
